name: Gnetum-leaf soup
summary: A clear soup of young lá bép shoots, also called rau nhíp, simmered with little seasoning and eaten hot with rice. It tastes clean, light, and sweet, the leaves gently chewy and nutty.
origin: A wild-vegetable soup of the Jrai, Ba Na, Xơ Đăng, and Ê Đê, common around Kon Tum, Gia Lai, and Đắk Lắk.
taste: Clean sweetness, a little crispness, and umami. Cooked, the leaf is gently chewy and nutty.
howToEat: The young shoots and tender leaves are washed and simmered. Eat it hot with rice, beside a stronger dish. The shoots are best in the rainy season, roughly May to October.
where: Around Kon Tum and across the Central Highlands.
seoDescription: A clear, sweet highland soup of young lá bép shoots, eaten hot with rice.
